paper.title_en: A unified topological framework for confinement and baryon structure
paper.abstract_en: Confinement, dynamical mass generation, and proton spin all depend strongly on infrared gluon dynamics, yet they are usually described by separate mechanisms. We propose that a Hopf-linked gluon configuration provides a common framework. In the Cho-Faddeev-Niemi representation of Yang-Mills fields, a root-flux vortex can separate into weight-flux constituents; a fundamental Wilson loop identifies each constituent as a center vortex. Monopole junctions and center flux can then form a finite-energy gluon knot. We propose that this linked monopole condensate surrounds the Y-shaped color-electric flux of three quarks. Its strong chromomagnetic field can promote chiral condensation and dynamical proton mass, whereas its time-dependent electric and magnetic fields carry gluon angular momentum. This picture unifies confinement and baryon structure while connecting them to proton mass and spin. Correlated lattice measurements of monopoles, center flux, linking, Dirac modes, and angular momentum can test the proposal.
